For any <MATH_0004> the object

These maps are compatible for varying <MATH_0009> and we obtain a comparison map

The right hand side is more recognizable as a kind of completion.
In general this comparison map is not an isomorphism.

Localization and derived completion<OWNARGEND_0001>Let <MATH_0001> be a ringed site.
Let <MATH_0002> be a finite type sheaf of
ideals. Let <MATH_0003> be the derived completion functor
of Proposition <REF_0001>. It follows
from the construction in the proof of the proposition that <MATH_0004>
is the derived completion of <MATH_0005> for any <MATH_0006>.
But we can also prove this as follows. From the definition
of derived complete objects it follows that <MATH_0007> is derived complete.
Thus we obtain a canonical map <MATH_0008>.
On the other hand, if <MATH_0009> is a derived complete object of
<MATH_0010>, then <MATH_0011> is a derived complete object of
<MATH_0012> by Lemma <REF_0002>.
Here <MATH_0013> is the localization morphism
(Modules on Sites, Section <REF_0003>).
Hence we also obtain a canonical
map <MATH_0014>. We omit the (formal) verification
that the adjoint of <MATH_0015> is the inverse of <MATH_0016>.
